newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-HINGIS TAKES FIRST SET FROM PIERCE 6-2.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS TAKES FIRST SET FROM PIERCE 6-2.

text.p: Swiss teenager Martina Hingis took the first set of the women's final of the Australian Open on Saturday, storming past 1995 champion Mary Pierce 6-2.
The 16-year-old Hingis, striving to become the youngest professional Grand Slam champion, used precision tennis to overcome Pierce's ground strokes.
Hingis showed composure beyond her years from the very first game, saving three break points on her own service. She broke Pierce in the next game and raced to a 5-0 lead.
Pierce took 20 minutes to get on the scoreboard, finally winning her third service game and then winning her fifth break point of the match to take the next game and trail 2-5.
But Hingis broke the French player in the next game to clinch the set.
Hingis took the second set 6-2, wrapping up the match in 59 minutes and becoming the youngest Grand Slam champion in the history of professional tennis.
The playful Swiss prodigy, who smiled broadly throughout the match, faced slightly more opposition in the final set but finally broke Pierce with a deft drop shot in the sixth game.
Hingis broke Pierce a second time in the eighth game to seize the match, taking the first of three match points with a forehand winner.
